items.headline: Microsoft Clarity (free website analytics) adds Agentic Analytics, Ask Clarity and wider Brand Agents
items.relevance: Websites: shows business owners which AI agents (Google, OpenAI, Anthropic operators) visit their site and what they do (searches, form submissions, bookings, checkout). Ask Clarity answers plain-English questions about visitor behaviour. Clarity is free.
items.angle: AI assistants are starting to visit websites on people's behalf. A free tool now shows you if they're on yours and whether they can finish a booking or enquiry.

facts.claim: Announced 4 November 2026: Agentic Analytics, Ask Clarity, Brand Agents expansion
facts.check: ppc.land and SERoundtable both date it 4 Nov 2026

facts.claim: Supported agents for Agentic Analytics are Google, OpenAI and Anthropic agent operators (not every AI agent)
Dashboard shows agent activity: searches, form submissions, logins, downloads, appointment bookings, checkout
Microsoft's figures come from its own analysis of 5.23 million agentic sessions across 230,511 projects, 13 Aug to 9 Sep 2026
facts.note: Vendor's own data, global not UK. Say so if used.

facts.claim: Brand Agents: eligible Shopify and WooCommerce merchants' products can appear in Copilot, Bing and MSN AI recommendations

items.caveats: Global rollout per Microsoft, but coverage limited to supported agents. Treat stats as Microsoft's own. Re-open the blog post before publishing to confirm nothing changed. Clarity needs disclosing in a privacy policy and cookie consent in the UK, so mention that if recommending people install it (check ICO cookie guidance).
items.note_2026-11-08: Used on LinkedIn only; still unused on Instagram/Facebook. Primary source re-checked 8 Nov: canonical URL https://clarity.microsoft.com/blog/clarity-connects-agents-LLMs-people/ (the ?p=10568 link errored). Ask Clarity is closed beta for retailers. Cookie consent: Clarity waits for a consent signal for UK/EEA/CH visitors since 31 Oct 2025 (learn.microsoft.com clarity consent-mode).

items.headline: Google releases the November 2026 core update (global, all languages, rollout may take up to 2 weeks)
items.relevance: Search: affects how every UK business website ranks in Google for up to a fortnight. Clear action from Google's own guidance: wait for it to finish, wait another full week, then compare in Search Console; small drops need no drastic action, large ones a deeper assessment; avoid quick fixes.

facts.claim: Incident began 2026-11-10 10:06 US/Pacific; 'Released the November 2026 core update, which applies globally and to all languages.' 'The rollout may take up to 2 weeks to complete.'
Google's guidance on core updates (wait a full week after completion, position 2 to 4 vs 4 to 29, avoid quick fixes, deleting content is a last resort)

items.caveats: Search Engine Land's article could not be opened (client error). Follow up when the dashboard shows the rollout has completed: a short 'it's finished, now check' Story or post would be a fair follow-up, not a repeat.

items.headline: OpenAI launches 'Businesses in ChatGPT' in beta: a Business Hub where a business can claim its profile and see mentions and website clicks
items.reason: Still not verified to the playbook standard on 11 Nov 14:33: OpenAI's own announcement (openai.com/index/introducing-businesses-chatgpt/) and help article (help.openai.com 'Setting up your business on ChatGPT') both refused to open again (client error). Also only partly relevant to UK firms yet: Business Agents are US only, and one UK outlet says local shop and restaurant claims are limited to existing US listings for now. One news post already went out today (Google core update). Re-check at the next run; if OpenAI's page still won't open, treat the OpenAI Developer Community announcement as the nearest primary text and say plainly what a UK business can and cannot do. 11 Nov 19:33 re-check: a search returned both OpenAI URLs (openai.com/index/introducing-businesses-chatgpt/ and help.openai.com/en/articles/20001635-setting-up-your-business-on-chatgpt) but both failed again (client error at the site), so OpenAI's own page has still not been read first-hand. Search Engine Roundtable (10 Nov, updated 11 Nov) and IT Brief UK (11 Nov) were opened and read again and agree with the facts below; neither names the UK. Still held.

facts.claim: Search Engine Roundtable (10 Nov 2026): claim by text or call to the main business number or DNS verification; analytics show mentions, profile views and clicks; OpenAI calls it beta; Business Agents start with eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the U.S.
IT Brief UK (11 Nov 2026): 'Business Hub is launching globally for eligible businesses wherever ChatGPT is available'; Business Agents US only; insights only above volume thresholds

OpenAI Developer Community, Announcements, 'Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT in beta' (posted 10 Nov 2026, opened and read 11 Nov): 'Claim your business, manage your information, and get insights on how people engage with you.' 'Eligible businesses located wherever ChatGPT is available can get started by claiming their business in Business Hub.' Business Agents: 'Available to eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the U.S.' 'We don't share people's conversations or Business Agent chats with businesses.' UK not named. No price stated. Replies from users mention a waitlist outside the US and a UK sole trader stuck on a VAT number field in the Persona identity check (user comments, not official).

PPC Land (11 Nov 2026, opened and read): 'OpenAI on November 10, 2026 opened Businesses in ChatGPT, a beta program'; reporting sits in Business Hub; claim a profile, correct details, add product feeds, see mention counts and click-throughs; Business Agents limited to eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the United States; no fee mentioned for claiming; government ID needed before editing; one non-US owner reported being put on a waitlist.

Tilio (UK agency, published 8 Nov, updated 10 Nov 2026, opened and read; sells setup services so treat as interested): says eligible UK online businesses can claim now, the 'service' claim option was marked coming soon in its UK test, and claims for local shops and restaurants are limited to existing US listings for now; verification by code to business email or phone, DNS TXT record or Shopify, plus Persona ID check.

items.caveats: UK not named by OpenAI in anything opened so far. Beta. Local shops and restaurants may not be able to claim in the UK yet (per Tilio, citing OpenAI's help centre, not read first-hand). Do not say 'now in the UK' unless OpenAI says so.

items.headline: Microsoft 365 outage: Exchange Online mailboxes (Outlook) unreachable from Thursday 12 Nov, with Teams, SharePoint, Copilot and other services affected; not resolved in any page read on the morning of 13 Nov
items.reason: Held at 08:33 (no first-hand Microsoft source, UK not named). Used at 13:27 the same day at Lee's request as a light-hearted post: by then the Evening Standard live blog had named UK organisations affected, and WLKY and Cyber Security News carried Microsoft's own words on restarting servers. Microsoft's status page and X posts still could not be opened. Follow up only if Microsoft publishes a post-incident report with something a business owner can act on.
items.relevance: Email is how most businesses receive website enquiries; clear action available (know the status page, make sure website forms also save enquiries somewhere other than the inbox).

facts.claim: SecurityWeek (12 Nov 2026, 3:55pm ET): Microsoft 365 'suffered a widespread outage Thursday'; users 'unable to connect to Exchange Online mailboxes'; incidents EX1550543 and MO1550821; no cyberattack evidence disclosed.

TechRadar live blog (12 Nov 2026): US reports from about 12:30pm ET; Downdetector Outlook reports peaked above 131,000; Microsoft said a core process on affected servers was being overwhelmed; limited recovery by about 6:05pm ET.

Business Standard (13 Nov 2026, 10:56 IST): outage continuing; Microsoft reversing a recent network configuration change; Microsoft EVP said it was not a cybersecurity breach; Downdetector reports from 74 countries.
IT-Connect (13 Nov 2026, 06:30 UTC): scope widened from the Americas to 'users in any region'; 'email delivery may be delayed'; no restoration time announced.

items.caveats: All Microsoft quotes are second-hand. Figures differ between outlets (131,000 vs 138,058 Downdetector peak). UK impact not stated anywhere that was read.

items.headline: Chrome now asks for permission before opening a site without HTTPS, on by default for all users (Google, 21 Oct 2026)
items.relevance: Hosting: a business site still on http now gets a permission prompt in Chrome the first time someone visits. Clear action: ask the host to switch on HTTPS. Outside the 7-day news window, so use it as a fact in a hosting post, not as news.

facts.claim: 'we have now rolled out a change where Chrome explicitly asks users for permission before making an insecure HTTP connection.' 'now we extended this protection to all users by default.' 'Chrome will ask the user to approve the use of HTTP the first time they visit the site.' 'Chrome will not warn again until the user has not visited the site for at least two weeks.' Not shown on sites that cannot get a publicly-trusted certificate (local addresses).
Chrome Help: 'Info or Not secure: The site doesn't use a private connection.' 'To resolve this issue, the site owner must secure the site and your data with HTTPS.'

second_sources: Help Net Security, 'Chrome puts insecure sites behind a permission prompt' (22 Oct 2026)
items.caveats: Global, not UK-specific. Google's 2025 announcement said 'Chrome 154 in October 2026'; do not quote a version or month beyond what the 21 Oct 2026 post says.
